I ran the code-standards review on your 3 uncommitted files. It found 10 problems: 2 errors and 8 warnings. One linter, ruff, couldn't run (details at the end).

```
Code standards: uncommitted changes, 3 files, 3.3s (ast-grep 1.9s, lizard 0.06s, jscpd 3.3s, oxlint 2.5s; ruff not run)

Errors
  app/api/loyalty_routes.py
    10  cs-env-outside-config     os.environ.get("LOYALTY_RATE", ...): read it from app.config.settings instead
  web/src/components/LoyaltyBadge.tsx
    10  eslint(no-debugger)       leftover `debugger;` statement   [fix]

Warnings
  app/api/loyalty_routes.py
    11  std-routes-delegate       the handler calls get_db().fetch_one(...) itself; pass get_db() to a loyalty_service function instead
    12  std-routes-delegate       a missing customer returns {"points": 0} with status 200; the service should raise LookupError, which routes map to 404
    14  std-routes-delegate       the gold-tier rate doubling is a business rule in the handler; move it into loyalty_service
  app/services/loyalty_service.py
     9  std-service-errors        find_customer returns None for a missing record; raise LookupError(f"customer {customer_id} not found")
    13  lizard/complexity         points_for: complexity 11 (limit 10)
  web/src/components/LoyaltyBadge.tsx
     6  std-components-use-api-modules  the component calls fetch() directly; add a typed function in web/src/api/customer.ts (or wherever customers live) and import it
    14  lizard/complexity         summarize: complexity 12 (limit 10)
```

**Tool problems:** ruff didn't run. It's in your Python dev dependencies (`ruff==0.17.1`), but there's no `uv.lock` or `poetry.lock`, so I didn't install it without asking first. When it runs, it will most likely flag `app/services/loyalty_service.py:1`, because `import json` is never used (rule F401). The tool hasn't confirmed that yet.

**Setup:** I ran `npm ci` to install oxlint from your `package-lock.json`. It didn't change any manifest or lockfile.

The four standards findings in the route and the service all have the same fix. Add a `loyalty_service.get_points(db, customer_id)` that looks up the customer, raises `LookupError` if it's missing, and applies the tier rules. The handler then reads the param, makes that one call, and returns the result. `find_customer` already does the lookup but nothing calls it yet; it can become that function once it raises instead of returning None.

Should I apply the fixes? Options are: install ruff (`uv sync`, which creates a lockfile), remove the `debugger`, refactor the route into the service, or all of these.
